claim: Apache Kafka preserves record ordering within an individual partition.
notes: Ordering is partition-scoped, not topic-wide.

claim: Apache Kafka guarantees a single global ordering of records across all partitions in a topic.
notes: Kafka ordering is not global across partitions.

claim: Using the same message key can cause Kafka records to be routed to the same partition, subject to the producer's partitioning behavior.
notes: Preserve the qualification around partitioner/configuration behavior.

claim: PostgreSQL SELECT supports SKIP LOCKED to skip rows that cannot immediately be locked.
notes: Documented SELECT locking behavior.

claim: PostgreSQL SKIP LOCKED provides a fully consistent view of all rows and is recommended for general-purpose queries.
notes: Documentation warns that SKIP LOCKED gives an inconsistent view and is suited to queue-like access patterns.

claim: PostgreSQL SKIP LOCKED can be useful for multiple consumers accessing a queue-like table without waiting on already-locked rows.
notes: Queue-like use is explicitly discussed in PostgreSQL documentation.

claim: A Kubernetes Deployment manages ReplicaSets as part of rolling out and maintaining application replicas.
notes: Core Deployment behavior.

claim: A Kubernetes Deployment directly manages Pods without using ReplicaSets.
notes: Deployments manage ReplicaSets, which manage Pods.

claim: A Kubernetes Service guarantees that every backend Pod is healthy before traffic is sent to it.
notes: Traffic eligibility depends on endpoint/readiness behavior and configuration; the absolute wording should not be accepted without qualification.

claim: In standard CPython builds, the Global Interpreter Lock allows only one thread at a time to execute Python bytecode in a process.
notes: Version/build context matters because free-threaded builds exist.

claim: The CPython GIL prevents all forms of concurrency in Python programs.
notes: I/O concurrency, multiprocessing, and other mechanisms remain possible.

claim: Python's multiprocessing module can use subprocesses to side-step limitations imposed by the Global Interpreter Lock for CPU-bound work.
notes: The Python docs explicitly describe multiprocessing as side-stepping the GIL by using subprocesses.

claim: Java's try-with-resources statement automatically closes resources that implement AutoCloseable when the statement finishes.
notes: Language/library documented behavior.

claim: Java volatile makes compound operations such as increment automatically atomic.
notes: Visibility/order guarantees do not make arbitrary read-modify-write operations atomic.

claim: ConcurrentHashMap allows concurrent retrievals and is designed for high expected concurrency on updates.
notes: JDK API semantics.

claim: Redis expires a key automatically after its configured time to live elapses, although the exact deletion moment can depend on expiration processing.
notes: Avoid interpreting TTL as a hard real-time deletion guarantee.

claim: Redis transactions provide rollback if a command executed inside EXEC fails.
notes: Redis transactions do not provide traditional rollback for runtime command errors.

claim: Redis pipelining reduces round-trip overhead by sending multiple commands without waiting for each individual response first.
notes: Core pipelining behavior.

claim: A Docker image is an immutable package used as a template for creating containers.
notes: Core image/container model.

claim: Docker containers always run a full independent guest operating-system kernel.
notes: Containers normally share the host kernel rather than each running a full guest kernel.

claim: A Docker bind mount exposes a host filesystem path inside a container and therefore couples the container to the host's filesystem layout.
notes: Host-path dependency is an important qualification.

claim: Amazon S3 provides strong read-after-write consistency for PUT and DELETE operations in all AWS Regions.
notes: Current S3 consistency model.

claim: Amazon S3 requires clients to wait for eventual consistency before reading a newly written object.
notes: Outdated behavior; modern S3 provides strong consistency.

claim: AWS Lambda execution environments may be reused across invocations, so code should not assume a fresh environment for every invocation.
notes: Reuse may occur but is not guaranteed.

claim: Google Cloud Pub/Sub provides at-least-once delivery by default.
notes: Default delivery semantics.

claim: Google Cloud Pub/Sub guarantees exactly-once delivery for every subscription without any configuration or regional constraints.
notes: Exactly-once delivery has explicit configuration and scope constraints.

claim: Google Cloud Pub/Sub ordering keys can preserve the order of messages that share the same ordering key when message ordering is enabled.
notes: Ordering requires enabling ordering and applies to messages sharing an ordering key.

claim: A distributed system cannot simultaneously guarantee consistency, availability, and partition tolerance during a network partition under the CAP model.
notes: Benchmark should require the network-partition qualification rather than accepting the simplistic 'pick any two' slogan.

claim: The CAP theorem means a distributed system must permanently choose exactly two of consistency, availability, and partition tolerance in all operating conditions.
notes: This common formulation is misleading; the tradeoff is specifically under partition.

claim: HTTP GET is defined as a safe method and is intended for information retrieval rather than requesting a state-changing action.
notes: Safety is semantic intent; servers can still have incidental side effects such as logging.
